nodes.label: CPD Sprint 2 — Design: Security wrapper + audit path + attendee identity
D1 — Restrict write_audit_event grant (revoke authenticated EXECUTE)
nodes.rationale: Closes the audit-authenticity gap from Sprint 1: a malicious authenticated user could forge a legitimately-chained row with false actor claims by calling write_audit_event directly via PostgREST. Every audited mutation instead becomes a SECURITY DEFINER fn ending in the audit write; the postgres-owned definer inherits audit_writer's EXECUTE, so legitimate paths are unaffected.

nodes.label: ADR Finding 1 — PostgREST RPCs run as separate transactions
nodes.rationale: An app-level wrapper calling write_audit_event after a mutation runs the audit write in a separate transaction, violating audit-insert-last-same-transaction; forces the SECURITY DEFINER gate→mutation→audit-write-LAST shape.

nodes.label: P2 — Global audit-chain lock discipline
nodes.rationale: The audit chain serializes all writes through one global advisory lock held for transaction duration; audited definer functions must complete slow work before the audit-write and have no side effects between audit-write and commit.

nodes.label: P3 — Behaviour-preserving TDD on rewritten surfaces
nodes.rationale: Check-in and event-publish are shipped surfaces converted to definer functions; capture current behaviour before rewrite, rewrite, re-run same tests, name any intentional delta (per-IP to per-event rate-limit change).
